new_findings.finding: The streaming processor's select is `biased` with the persistence channel first and breaks on `None` without checking the executor's JoinHandle. On an executor panic, CleanupGuard::drop (execute.rs:69-82) spawns queue destroy, which removes the manager's Arc (streaming/event_queue/manager.rs:456-458), the last holder of the writer and so of the persistence Sender; recv() then returns None and the loop breaks before executor_panicked() runs. The task is never marked Failed and no webhook is told - undoing the D-03 fix in that interleaving.
new_findings.scenario: Current-thread runtime (#[tokio::main(flavor="current_thread")], and every #[tokio::test]): tokio's current_thread scheduler queues FIFO (tokio-1.54.1 current_thread/mod.rs:355-356), and the destroy task is spawned during the harness's drop of the panicked future, before the JoinHandle wakes the processor, so destroy runs first: likely every streaming panic leaves the task Submitted/Working. Multi-thread: the LIFO slot usually runs the processor first, but a stealing worker can run destroy first (narrow race). Blocking path: same shape when the executor is Spawned (multi-thread); the Inline path (single worker) is safe because catch_unwind returns Ready(false) in the same poll. With SQL + claims the reaper ends the task after a TTL; in memory it stays Working forever and a resubscriber waits forever (subscribe_max_idle None). No test covers it: processor_tests call executor_panicked directly; handler/messaging/tests.rs:77 checks only token release. Fix: on recv() == None while !executor_done, await handle_fuse and call executor_panicked on Err (same in SyncCollector::run).

new_findings.finding: A WebSocket call enqueues its frame with `write_tx.send(..).await` on a 64-slot channel before any timeout starts; request_timeout/send_timeout bound only the wait for the reply (:818). The writer task's ws_writer.send() is untimed. When the peer stops reading (zero window: a server wedged by D-07, a frozen process, or a half-open path once the send buffer fills), the writer blocks, the channel fills, and every later call on the connection hangs with no bound; when the socket finally dies the blocked callers get Transport('writer task closed'), non-retryable.
new_findings.scenario: Client sends to an agent whose WS read loop is pinned (D-07) or a half-open connection (D-08): after ~64 queued frames plus the socket buffer, GetTask/SendMessage calls never return (until ~15 min retransmission timeout on half-open; forever on a live-but-not-reading peer). Fix: put the enqueue under the same deadline (timeout around send + reply) or try_send and fail fast as retryable.

new_findings.finding: The new per-destination delivery bound (push_max_in_flight_per_host, 64) is keyed by the URL's host name (and canonical IP literal), not by the resolved address, so N names that resolve to one IP (a wildcard DNS record) are N destinations. A caller can aim up to push_max_in_flight (512) concurrent deliveries at one third-party IP, 8x the intended per-destination bound.
new_findings.scenario: Anonymous agent with push enabled; attacker registers webhooks at a1..aN.evil.example, all A records pointing at a victim; the agent opens up to 512 concurrent connections to the victim. Overlaps the F-slice rows N-SEC-6/SEC-14 that ee0a4c4 closed; key the per-destination semaphore by the resolved address rather than the name (the gate runs before the sender resolves, so this means resolving in the gate, or taking the per-address permit inside HttpPushSender after url_guard::resolve).
